title: Changing the Accountant of an Estonian Company

fields.content_blocks_0_content:
Companies stay for years with an accountant who answers once a week, misses deadlines and keeps sending new extra charges, because switching feels complicated and risky. In reality, changing your accountant in Estonia is a clear procedure. The risk is not the switch itself, but doing it without a checklist and losing data, access rights or an unclosed period.

Documents and accounts belong to the company, not to the accountant. Your task is to take them back completely and on time. Ours is to take over the books, check what really happened in them and carry on without a break in tax returns.

We take over Estonian companies from other accountants and services, including online platforms and cases where the previous accountant has stopped responding. We give you a handover checklist, request whatever is missing ourselves, reconcile open periods against EMTA data and quote a price only once we see the real state of the books.
fields.content_blocks_3_content:
Key facts

Topic Practical explanation
Who owns the documents The company: source documents, ledgers, reports and exports are its property
Retention period 7 years under the Accounting Act — an obligation of the company, not of the accountant
When you can switch At any time; it is easier after closing a month, quarter or financial year
Notice period As set in the contract with the previous accountant — check it before you decide
e-MTA access A management board member grants and revokes rights online; the previous accountant loses access immediately
Liability for the past Errors from earlier periods remain the company's errors — they will have to be corrected anyway
Break in tax returns Not acceptable: TSD by the 10th and KMD by the 20th continue without pauses
If the previous accountant does not respond The core of the books is rebuilt from banks, payment services and e-MTA
Accounting software If the software account is in the accountant's name, the data must be exported before the contract ends
fields.content_blocks_4_steps_title: How to switch to us: 4 steps
fields.content_blocks_4_step_1: Send a request. Tell us the registration code, who keeps the books now, up to which period they are closed and why you want to change accountant.
fields.content_blocks_4_step_2: Get an assessment and a checklist. We check the company in the register, agree on the switch date and give you a list of what to collect from the previous accountant.
fields.content_blocks_4_step_3: Sign the contract and switch access. A board member grants us rights in e-MTA and revokes the previous accountant's rights online in a few minutes. Banks and payment services get read-only access.
fields.content_blocks_4_step_4: We take over the books. We load the data, reconcile opening balances with banks and e-MTA, close loose ends and keep filing tax returns without a break.
fields.content_blocks_4_step_description: If the previous accountant does not respond, start with step 1: we will rebuild the core of the books from bank and EMTA data and send a request for the handover of documents in parallel.

fields.content_blocks_7_title_right: When it is time to change your accountant
fields.content_blocks_7_text_right:
Changing your accountant is not a conflict but a management decision. Five signs that it is time to make it:

  • You keep the deadlines, not your accountant. You remind them about tax returns, not the other way round. Or you learn about a fine from a letter from the register.
  • Answers take days. A simple question about a payout or an invoice waits a week for an answer, and a complex one never gets one.
  • The price grows unpredictably. Every return, every transaction above the limit and every question is billed separately, and the annual total ends up several times higher than the tariff.
  • No expertise for your business model. The accountant does not work with OSS, Stripe, multi-currency accounts, crypto assets or payments to non-residents.
  • You do not understand what has been filed. There is no monthly summary, tax liabilities are not visible, and the annual report arrives for signature on the last day.
fields.content_blocks_8_title_left: Key insight: data is lost not in a conflict but in a “quiet” exit
fields.content_blocks_8_text_left:
Most often a company loses data not because the accountant withholds it, but because nobody thought of taking it back.

  • Software in the accountant's name. If the subscription to the accounting software is registered to the accountant or their firm, access to the accounting history disappears when the contract ends. A full export must be obtained before termination.
  • e-MTA rights not revoked. The previous accountant keeps access to the company's tax data until a board member revokes the rights.
  • Documents only in the accountant's mailbox. Invoices and contracts you sent by email may never have been entered into the books.

Practical takeaway: before giving notice, get a full export from the software, an archive of source documents and copies of all filed returns. Then switch all access on the same day.
fields.content_blocks_9_title_right: Key insight: switching is a free audit of the past
fields.content_blocks_9_text_right:
When taking over the books, a diligent accountant always reconciles the opening balances: banks, taxes, settlements with counterparties. This is exactly the step where the previous accountant's errors surface: unreported VAT on purchases of foreign services, owner's expenses without documents, a “zero” report despite real transactions.

Liability for past periods does not pass to the new accountant, but it does not disappear either: it stays with the company. It is better to find the errors during the switch and correct them yourself than to hear about them from EMTA. We show what we find in the report on the state of the books and propose a correction plan.

• Monthly accounting — the main format after the switch

fields.content_blocks_11_content:
Changing your accountant: how it works in practice

Checklist: what to collect from the previous accountant

What Why
Full export from the accounting software General ledger and journal entries for the current and previous year
Trial balance at the switch date Opening balances for the new books
Fixed asset register Depreciation and residual value
Lists of receivables and payables Who owes whom at the switch date
Copies of filed TSD, KMD, VD and OSS returns Reconciliation with e-MTA data
Reconciliation of the e-MTA prepayment account Tax liabilities and overpayments
Payroll and holiday data If there are employees
Archive of source documents Invoices, receipts, contracts — kept for 7 years
Accounting policies (internal accounting rules) Methods to continue or change deliberately
Open EMTA and register requests So that no response deadline is missed

Access: what to switch on the day of the switch

  1. e-MTA — a board member grants rights to the new accountant and revokes them from the previous one.
  2. Banks and payment services — new read-only or export access; close the old access.
  3. Accounting software — transfer the subscription to the company or get a full export.
  4. Mailbox for documents — give suppliers and services the new address for invoices.

When is the best time to switch

Technically, at any time. It is most convenient after closing a month, and even more so after closing a quarter or financial year. The worst moment is a week before 30 June if the annual report is not ready yet: in that case, first agree who will file it.

If the previous accountant does not respond or does not hand over documents

The documents belong to the company, and the request to hand them over is sent in writing with a reasonable deadline. While there is no answer, we rebuild the core of the books from bank statements, payment services and e-MTA data, and download missing invoices from supplier accounts. Work on the company continues without a break in tax returns.

How long the switch takes

Situation Approximate time
The books are closed and the export has been received 1–2 weeks
The export is incomplete and documents need to be collected 2–4 weeks
The previous accountant does not respond Depends on the scope of restoration

fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_0_question: Can I change accountant in the middle of the year?
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_0_answer: Yes, at any time. It is easier after closing a month or quarter. Tax returns continue without a break, and the annual report for the year of the switch is prepared by the new accountant.
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_1_answer: The company. Source documents, ledgers, exports and copies of reports are the company's property, and it must keep them for 7 years.
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_2_question: What if the accountant does not hand over documents or does not respond?
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_2_answer: Send a written request with a deadline and, in parallel, start rebuilding the books from banks, payment services and e-MTA. This way the filing of returns is not interrupted.
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_3_question: How do I remove the previous accountant's access?
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_3_answer: A board member revokes their rights in e-MTA online and closes access to banks and payment services. It is best done on the day of the switch.
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_4_question: Do I need to notify the register about the change of accountant?
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_4_answer: No. The accountant is not entered in the Commercial Register. Only access rights and the contract change.
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_5_question: Is the new accountant liable for the previous one's errors?
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_5_answer: No, but the errors remain the company's errors. We show what we find during the takeover and propose a correction plan.
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_6_question: Can I move from an online platform to a regular accountant?
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_6_answer: Yes. The key is to get a full data export and copies of filed reports before the subscription ends.
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_7_question: How much does the switch cost?
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_7_answer: It depends on the state of the books: whether they are closed, whether the export is complete and whether corrections are needed. We quote the takeover price after the assessment, and monthly service is a fixed amount.
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_8_question: How long does the switch take?
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_8_answer: If the books are closed and the export has been received, usually 1–2 weeks. With incomplete data, longer.
